title: [FR] Configurable Hashing Algorithm/Using MLFlow in FIPS environment
body: I am testing MLflow in a FIPS-enabled environment and encounter FIPS errors because `file_store.py` calls `hashlib.md5(dataset_name.encode("utf-8"))`. Our project cannot disable FIPS, and I do not know of another way around the limitation. I would like the backend hashing algorithm to be configurable so that users can select an alternative algorithm.

symptoms_visible: When I test MLflow in our FIPS-enabled environment, I encounter FIPS errors associated with its use of MD5.
Our project cannot disable FIPS, so this prevents us from using MLflow as it currently behaves.
N0.label: N0 FIPS MD5 incompatibility reported

symptoms_visible: When I try to save a model through the Python SDK, I get FIPS-related warnings while communicating with an MLflow server pod.
N1.label: N1 deployment context supplied

symptoms_visible: With MLflow 2.7.1, sklearn autologging warns that the request to `/api/2.0/mlflow/runs/log-inputs` received too many 500 responses.
At the same time, the MLflow server pod logs an exception for the `log-inputs` POST endpoint.
N2.label: N2 exact setup and errors collected

symptoms_visible: Running the supplied client code against the container on a FIPS-enabled RHEL 8 host reproduces the autologging request failure and server exception.
N3.label: N3 FIPS reproduction requirements established

symptoms_visible: When I test the proposed handling of the hash call, the FIPS-related issue no longer occurs in my check.
N4.label: N4 candidate behavior checked in FIPS environment

symptoms_visible: The proposed non-security hash handling avoids the FIPS-related error in my test, but I have not confirmed which released MLflow version includes the change.
N_terminal.label: terminal candidate confirmed but released version unverified

question_patterns: How can we reproduce the error, and can it be reproduced with Docker?
What operating system and FIPS-enabled environment are you using?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I installed MLflow with pip in a Python-based container and ran it as a pod on a RHEL 8.8-based Kubernetes cluster with FIPS enabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This also happens on a regular non-FIPS machine, and disabling FIPS makes no difference.
The same setup is on a FIPS-enabled RHEL 8 VM rather than Kubernetes.

question_patterns: Is the Python code running in the same container as the MLflow server?
How is the client communicating with the server?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The MLflow server runs in one pod, and I communicate with it from another pod in the same cluster.

question_patterns: What operation produces the error?
When do the FIPS warnings appear?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I try to save the model using the Python SDK, I get warnings regarding FIPS in the container.

edges.comment: Issue comments c1-c2, reporter's deployment only: the maintainer asks for reproduction details, and the reporter identifies the Python container, RHEL 8.8 FIPS cluster, separate pods, and model-saving operation.

question_patterns: Which Python base image and MLflow version are you using?
Can you provide the exact package versions from the failing container?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Dockerfile uses a Python 3.9 base image, and requirements install MLflow 2.7.1 with pip.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same failure occurs with a Python 3.10 base image and the same MLflow version.

question_patterns: What command starts the MLflow server?
Can you share the container CMD?
Can you paste the exact client-side error?
What does sklearn autologging report when the operation fails?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The client warns that sklearn autologging encountered an unexpected error. Its request to `http://my-kubeflow-service/api/2.0/mlflow/runs/log-inputs` reaches the retry limit because of too many 500 responses.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The request never reaches the server because DNS resolution for the service name fails.

question_patterns: What appears in the MLflow server log at the same time?
Can you share the server-side traceback?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The server pod logs `ERROR mlflow.server: Exception on /api/2.0/mlflow/runs/log-inputs [POST]` followed by a Flask traceback through the MLflow server handler.

question_patterns: Can you share the Dockerfile?
How is MLflow installed and which user runs it in the container?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Dockerfile starts from `python:3.9`, creates an `mlflow` user, installs `requirements.txt` with pip as that user, adds `/home/<user>/.local/bin` to PATH, and starts `mlflow server --host 0.0.0.0`.

question_patterns: Can you share the client code that triggers the failure?
What is the smallest workflow you have that produces the error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My client sets the tracking and registry URIs to the service, enables `mlflow.autolog()`, loads the sklearn diabetes dataset, and fits a `RandomForestRegressor`. That triggers the warning.

edges.comment: Issue comments c4-c6, reporter's systems only: the reporter supplies MLflow 2.7.1, Python 3.9, the client reproducer, raw client/server errors, and the requested Dockerfile.

question_patterns: How should we run this Dockerfile to reproduce the error?
Are there any required host settings beyond building and running the container?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Build the container, run it on a RHEL 8 machine with FIPS enabled, and run the client code from that machine or another FIPS-enabled RHEL machine. Any basic RHEL 8 VM with FIPS enabled should suffice.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The error is reproducible inside the image on any host and does not depend on whether the host has FIPS enabled.
The Kubernetes namespace and service name are different in another deployment.

question_patterns: Which part of the example appears to trigger the failure?
Does the error happen before or after enabling MLflow autologging?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I believe it is the `autolog` feature in particular that trips the error.

edges.comment: Issue comments c7-c10, reporter's reproduction chain: a FIPS-enabled RHEL 8 host is essential, and the reporter identifies autologging as the operation that appears to trigger the endpoint failure.

question_patterns: Could you install the proposed PR build and rerun the same workflow in your FIPS environment?
Please test the candidate change against the same reproducer and report only what happens.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The `usedforsecurity` flag appears to get around the issue.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I installed the proposed PR build, but the same FIPS error and repeated 500 responses still occur.
The proposed build completes the same autologging operation without the FIPS error on a second FIPS-enabled RHEL 8 VM.

question_patterns: Would SHA-1 work in your environment?
Do you expect SHA-1 to remain usable under your FIPS requirements?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: `hashlib.sha1` should work as well, though FIPS is looking to move away from it at some point, so the same flag may eventually need to be supplied to SHA-1.

edges.comment: Issue comments c19-c22, reporter's candidate check: the maintainer supplies a PR installation command, and the reporter later states that the non-security flag appears to avoid the issue. This is pre-landing test evidence, not proof that a released MLflow package contains the change.

solution.intent: Keep MLflow's existing non-cryptographic MD5-derived identifiers while constructing affected MD5 hashes with `usedforsecurity=False`, allowing them in FIPS-restricted Python environments without requiring users to disable FIPS or select a different digest.
solution.concrete_example: For MLflow hash calls that are only producing non-security identifiers, construct the MD5 object with `hashlib.md5(data, usedforsecurity=False)`. The reporter states that this handling appears to avoid the FIPS issue. Ask them to rerun the original autologging workflow after installing an MLflow build that contains the change.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the FIPS environment, failing endpoint behavior, MD5 call site, and the observation that the proposed flag avoids the issue. The conclusion that MLflow uses this digest only as a non-security identifier—and therefore should retain MD5 compatibility while setting `usedforsecurity=False`—is the maintainer's technical determination.

edges.comment: Issue comments c15-c22 establish the accepted technical direction: MLflow's MD5 usage is not security-sensitive, Python 3.9 supports the keyword, and the reporter says the flag avoids the issue. The thread does not contain the reporter's confirmation on a subsequently released MLflow version; c23 explicitly asks which release contains the fix, so the terminal remains unverified from the user's perspective.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: a FIPS-enabled Python environment blocks MLflow's default MD5 construction even though the affected digest is used as a non-security identifier.
Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: the FIPS-enabled RHEL 8 environment, the MD5 call site, the autologging `log-inputs` failure, and the reporter's candidate-build observation.

The technical fix must mark affected non-security MD5 construction with `usedforsecurity=False`; switching to SHA-1 or introducing a configurable algorithm is not required by the final accepted approach.
Must not recommend disabling FIPS, because the reporter's project cannot do so.
Must ask the reporter to rerun the original workflow on an MLflow build containing the change and must not claim that a released version is verified until that retest occurs.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical platform user who can build containers, operate Kubernetes workloads on RHEL, provide Python reproducers and logs, and install a package directly from a proposed pull request, but is new to MLflow internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and practical; provides requested environment details and code promptly, answers direct technical questions concisely, and is candid when a result is tentative.
